WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS  
Halting of Trains at Alam Nagar Station  
†*261. SHRI BANWARI LAL KANCHHAL: Will the Minister  of 
RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether he is aware of demonstration under the lead ership of Uttar 
Pradesh Jan Kalyan Samiti for halting of various tr ains at Alam Nagar 
railway station in Lucknow; 
(b) whether his Ministry is considering the 21-point de mand letter 
submitted by them; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [16 March, 2007] 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether Government would consider halt of various trains at Alam Nagar 
station in public interest; and 
(e) if so, by when and if not, the reason therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI LALU PRASAD): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) to (e) The demands have been examined and the position is as 
under:— 
(1) Stoppage of 4369/4370 Singrauli-Bareilly Triven i Express, 4511/ 
4512 Allahabad-Saharanpur Nauchandi Express, 2229/2 230 
Lucknow-New Delhi Lucknow Mail 4265/4266 Varanasi-D ehradun 
Express, 3009/3010 Howrah-Dehradun Doon Express, 30 05/3006 
Howrah-Amritsar Mail, 3151/3152 Kolkata-Jammu Tawi Sealdah 
Express and 5609/5610 Guwahati-Lalgarh Avadh Assam Express 
at Alam Nagar Station:  
4266 Dehradun-Varanasi Express is already stopping at Alamnagar from 
July, 2005. Stoppage of the remaining trains is not  feasible as well as not 
commercially justified. 
(2) Provision of Bigger waiting hall, waiting room at Platform No. 1 and 
shed on Platform No. 2 at Alam Nagar:  
Waiting Room at the station has been provided. Bigger waiting hall and shed 
at platform No.2 has been sanctioned. 
(3) Reconstruction of toilets on Platform No. 1 and  construction of 
toilets on Platform No. 2:  
Reconstruction of toilets on Platform No.1 and prov ision of toilets on 
Platform No.2 are being done. 
(4) Provision of water cooler and Public Call Offic e (PCO) at Alam 
Nagar.  
Water cooler will be provided during the summer of 2007. Allotment of PCO 
Booth is under process. 
(5) Lengthening of platfonv at Alam Nagar and Lachh manpur:  
Lengthening of Platform Nos. 2 & 3 at Alam Nagar ha s been sanctioned. 
Lengthening of platforms at Lachhmanpur is not required at present. 
2 

[16 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(6) Stoppage of all Mail/Express trains at Manak Nagar station:  
Stoppage of all the Mail/Express trains at Manak Nagar is not feasible as well 
as not commercially justified. 
(7) Running of the circular trains to Lucknow from Malihabad:  
Extension of Circular trains to Malihabad is not feasible as these trains runs 
on electrified traction and Lucknow-Malihabad secti on is a non-electrified 
section. Moreover, it is not commercially justified. 
(8) Doubling of Railway Track between Utrahtia-Prayag:  
The doubling on this section is not considered necessary for the present. 
(9) Morning train at 7:30hrs from Lucknow-Charbagh to Shahajahanpur.  
Introduction of additional train on the section is not feasible due to 
operational and resource constraints. 
(10) 1/2 Lucknow- Varanasi Passenger divided into t wo parts from Rae 
Bareli one part from Lucknow to Varanasi and the ot her Part from 
via Unchahar:  
Bifurcation and diversion of a portion of 1LV/2LV L ucknow-Varanasi 
Passenger from Rae Bareli is not operationally feasible. 
(11) New Express train from Lucknow Charbagh to All ahabad between 
10:00 hours to 12:00 hours or 3005/3006 Howrah-Amri tsar Mail be 
diverted via Allahabad- Unchahar on 3 days a week:  
Introdcution of new train between Lucknow and Allah abad is not 
operationally feasible due to terminal and line cap acity constraints. Diversion 
of 3005/3006 Howrah-Amritsar Mail is not feasible. 
(12) Provision of over bridge at Jagjivan Ram Railw ay Protection Force 
training center Railway crossing and Alam Nagar Rai lway crossing 
and RDSO Railway crossing:  
One Road Over Bridge (ROB) near Jagjivan Ram Railway Protection Force 
Training center in lieu of Level Crossing No. 218 A  (Hardoi Crossing) on 
Lucknow-Hardoi line and Level Crossing No. 1B (Kanpur Crossing) on 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [16 March, 2007] 
Lucknow-Kanpur town has been sanctioned in 2004-05 on cost sharing basis. 
The Plan was agreed by State Government and Estimate is under finalisation. 
ROBs and RDSO Level Crossing No. 2A and at Alam Nag ar Level 
Crossing No. 221A have not yet been sanctioned as the State Government has not 
sponsored requisite proposals under extent rules. 
(13) Increase the number of General Bogies in long distance Mail/ 
Express trains:  
It has been announced in the Railway Budget 2007-08  that atleast 6 
General Class coaches will be provided in every newly introduced train except 
Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Jan Shatabdi Expresses. 
(14) To provide family planning concession to passengers having family 
planning certificate:  
Examined but not found desirable at present. 
(15) Dalmau Railway Station (NR) be connected with Fatehpur (NCR) 
Railway station by Rail line:  
The proposed link will involve construction of bridge over river Ganga. The 
rail link between North Central Railway and Northern Railway is already available at 
Kanpur and Allahabad. Further, link is not considered necessary at present. 
(16) Reduction in the penalty of without ticket fro m Rs. 250 
to Rs.50:  
The minimum penalty of Rs.250 is serving as a deter rent for ticketless 
travellers. 
(17) Permission to daily passengers to travel in Mail/Express trains:  
Daily passengers are supposed to travel by suburban and ordinary non-suburban 
trains. However, daily passengers holding Season Tickets are allowed to travel 
in unreserved coaches of certain Mail/Express train s. This permission cannot 
be granted in all Mail/Express trains. 
(18) Coach number be indicated on the reserved coaches: 
Railways ensure that coach number boards painted with the coach 
4 

[16 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
numbers wz.A1.A2, ....... AS1.AS2 ........ S1.S2, S3 ....... etc. in the prescribed 
size and shape, are invariably fixed on both sides of the reserved coaches 
before the rake leaves the pite line at the primary maintenance end. 
(19) Proper maintenance and re-construction of toil ets on the stations 
between Lucknow to Prayag, Lucknow to Kanpurand Luc know to 
Shahajahanpur.  
Toilets on various stations are being maintained an d renovated on 
condition basis and repaired as and when required. 
(20) Announcement of the name of the station when t he trains stop at 
the stations where announcement facilities are-available:  
The suggestion is good one. Efforts will be made to implement the same. 
(21) Removal of animals loitering on the platform a t Lucknow-Charbagh 
Station:  
Efforts are always made with the help of the local administration to check 
this menace on the platforms. 
TPDS beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh  
*262. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of CON SUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the details the beneficiaries under TPDS under APL, BPL and AAY in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh during the last five years, year-wise and district-wise; 
(b) the number of Fair Price Shops that are distributin g foodgrains in the 
State to those beneficiaries; 
(c) whether it is a fact that Government monitors PDS. on monthly-basis; 
(d) if so, the details of mechanism under which Government monitors PDS 
on monthly-basis; 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [16 March, 2007] 
(e) whether the States are mandated to submit from- 'C as required 
under PDS Order, 2001; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof with regard to Andhra Pradesh? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) A Statement of beneficiaries 
under .TPDS under APL, BPL and AAY as received from the State of Andhra 
Pradesh is annexed (See below). 
(b) 41505 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. PDS is operated under the joint r esponsibility of the 
Central and the State Governments. The Central Gove rnment has the 
responsibility for procurement, storage, transportation and bulk allocation of 
foodgrains, etc. The responsibility for effectively distributing the same to the 
consumers through the network of Fair Price Shops ( FPSs) lies with the State 
Governments. The operational responsibilities including allocation within the State, 
identification of families below poverty line, issue of ration cards, supervision and 
monitoring the functioning of Fair Price Shops rest with the State Governments. 
For maintaining supply and securing availability an d distribution of 
foodgrains under the PDS, the Central Government ha s notified PDS 
(Control) Order, 2001 on 31.08.2001. The procedure for monitoring of the Public 
Distribution System (PDS) including the functioning  of the Fair-Price Shops 
(FPSs) by the State Governments has been prescribed  in Annexe to the PDS 
(Control) Order, 2001. Proviso 6(4) of the Annexe, stipulates that the State 
Governments shall ensure a periodic system of repor ting and the complete 
information in this regard shall be sent in the prescribed form as follows: 
(i) By fair price shops in the District Authorities by the 7th of the month 
following the month for which allocation is made in Form 'A'. 
(ii) By the District authorities to State Government by the 15th of the month 
following the month for which allocation is made in Form 'B'. 
(iii) By the State Government to the Central Government by the end of the 
month following the month for which allocation is made in Form 'C. 
(e) and (f) Yes, Sir. The State Government have furnished information in form 
"C to the Central Government upto October, 2006. 
6 

[16 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA

Expansion of Crop Insurance Policy  
*263. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any proposal to expand the Crop 
Insurance Policy as per the recommendation of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan Committee; 
and 
(b) whether women are being included in the farm insurance scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) No, 
Sir. The recommendations of the National Commission on Farmers headed by Dr. 
M.S. Swaminathan are being examined by the Government. 
(b) Yes, Sir. Under the existing National Agricultu ral Insurance Scheme 
(NAIS), women farmers are also eligible for availing the benefit.

THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI LALU PRASAD):(a) According to 
Entry No. 2 of the State List of the Constitution o f India. 'Police' (including 
Railways and village Police), is a State subject. P revention of crime, 
registration of cases, their investigation and main tenance of law and order in 
Railway premises as well as on running trains are, therefore, the statutory 
responsibility of the State Police. The State Police have a separate wing called the 
Government Railway Police for dealing with all matters relating to law and order 
on the Railways. Prevention and detection of crime is the constitutional 
responsibility of the State Governments, and as suc h, Ministry of Railways 
has to depend largely on them for control of crime over Railways. 
The Government Railway Police (under the State/Unio n Territory 
Governments) co-ordinate the security arrangements as per the requirements 
and levels of security threats, their nature etc. The Railways actively assist in 
aspects pertaining to the Railways in order to facilitate smooth train operations 
and transportation of passengers, parcels and goods in such situations. 
However, to provide better security to the travelling passengers in trains and 
passenger areas, the Railway Protection Force Act, 1957 and the Railway Act, 
1989 have been amended in 2003 to enable the Railways, through the Railway 
Protection Force - to effectively supplement the ef forts of the State/Union 
Territory Governments in controlling crime on the Railways. As per amendment 
in the RPF Act, 1957 the RPF personnel have been entrusted the responsibilities 
of better protection and security of railway property, passenger area and passengers 
and for matters connected therewith with effect from 01.07.2004. The Railway 
Protection Force staff are being deployed to escort trains and are also deployed 
in the passenger area to augment the efforts of the State Police. By amendment in the 
Railways Act, Railway Protection Force have also been empowered to deal with 
certain minor offences affecting train operations such as Alarm chain pulling, roof 
travel, touting, ticket less travel, unauthorized entry etc. (except Subotage related 
offences under Sections 150 to 152) with effect from July 2004. The objective 
was to ensure that the State Police (Government Rai lway Police) get more 
manpower and time to handle heinous offences such a s Terrorist activities, 
Murder, Dacoity, Robbery, Rape, Sabotage, Train Wre cking etc. under the 
provisions of Indian Penal Code, the Railways Act and other Laws of the land.

ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Nationa l Family Health 
Survey-Ill (NFHS-III) has been conducted in the yea r 2005-06. The survey 
has collected information on Mortality, marriage & Fertility, Family Planning, 
Maternal and Child Health, Immunization of children , Treatment seeking 
behaviour for childhood diseases like diarrhoea & a cute respiratory infection, 
child feeding practices, Nutritional status of chil dren and adults, prevalence of 
anemia among children and adults, obesity among men & women, Knowledge

women's empowerment, use of iodated salt, family li fe education, prevalence

Some of the key findings of the survey paint a mixe d picture of India's 
health. On the one hand, institutional delivery and  maternity care has 
improved, unmet need for family planning has reduce d, women are having 
fewer children, infant mortality has dropped; overa ll immunization coverage 
of children has improved and knowledge about HIV/AIDS has improved in the 
seven-year period since the last NFHS survey (1998- 99). On the other hand, 
anaemia and malnutrition are still widespread among  children and adults. 
And, in an odd juxtaposition, more adults, especial ly urban women, are 
overweight or obese.

Health Mission (NRHM), launched in April, 2005. The  national Rural Health 
Mission seeks to provide accessible, affordable and  quality health care to the 
rural population, especially the vulnerable section . It also seeks to reduce 
maternal mortality ratio from the current level of 301 (as per Registrar 
General of India's SRS Report 2001-03) to 100 per 1 00,000 live births and 
infant mortality from current level of 58 (as per R egistrar General of India's 
SRS Report 2005) to 30 per 1000 live births and the  Total fertility level from 
2.9 (as per Registrar General of India's SRS Report  2005) to 2.1 within the 
seven year period of the Mission, ending in 2012. N RHM has pro-poor focus 
and integrates all the stand-alone programmes into a single composite

*276.SHRI KANJIBHAI PATE'L: Will the Minister of HE ALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the number of institution al deliveries in the 
country has reached 50 per cent mark; 
(b) if so, the reasons for non-coverage of the remaining 50 per cent; and 
(c) the measures being taken to raise the percentage of such deliveries? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI 
RAMDOSS): (a) to (b) Institutional delivery rate for the country is estimated at 
40.7% as per the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) conducted in 2005-06. 
The reasons for low institutional delivery are multi factoral that include inter-alia 
various socio-economic and cultural factors, lack o f health infrastructure 
alongwith poor accessibility and utilization of ava ilable services at the health 
facilities. 
(c) With a view to encourage pregnant women, especially those in the rural 
and underserved areas, avail facilities provided by health institutions for delivery, 
the Government of India has launched a programme for safe motherhood namely 
the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) under National Rur al Health Mission 
(NRHM.). The scheme addresses quality maternal care  during pregnancy, 
delivery and immediate post-delivery period with appropriate referral transport 
along with cash assistance to pregnant women, to meet the cost of delivery. The 
scheme focuses on poor pregnant women, including wo men from SC/ST 
families, whose the level of institutional delivery  is low. Since the 
implementation of the scheme in April 2005, there has been manifold increase in 
the number of beneficiaries availing this facility and thus increasing institutional 
deliveries. As against 5.7 lakh JSY beneficiaries i n the year 2005-06, around 
21 lakh women have taken benefit of this scheme upto December 2006, during the 
current financial year. 
The following initiatives have also been taken under the National Rural Health 
Mission (NRHM) to improve facilities for institutional deliveries: 
Organizing Village Health & Nutrition Day at every Anganwadi center at 
least once every month to provide maternal and child health

• Equipping 50% of all Primary Health Centers with 24 -hours delivery 
services, by 2010. 
• Strengthening of sub-centers to improve service delivery by providing united 
fund of Rs. 10,000 each. 
• Appointment of Accredited Social Health Activist (A SHA) in every 
village for every 1000 population who will facilitate pregnant women in 
accessing health facilities for antenatal care, institutional delivery and post-
natal checks ups. 
• Ensuring quality MCH services by implementing the I ndian Public 
Health Standards (IPHS) for Primary Healthcare Faci lities, by 
providing infrastructure, specialized man-power and equipment. 
• Training of Medical doctors in emergency obstetric care and 
administering anesthesia for cesarian section. 
• Ensuring skilled attendance at every birth.

ART Center has been set up under NACP in Orissa. Rs. 19.45 crore was allocated

2023. SHRI M. V. MYSURAREDDY: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that due to enforcement of Kyoto Protocol, the carbon 
trade is becoming one of the hottest commodities in the international market; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that there are two system s in the carbon trade 
i.e. allowing emission credits to be traded between two countries (joint 
implementation) and allowing companies to earn cred its by paying for 
emission, reducing and clean energy projects (clean  development 
mechanism) in developing countries. 
(c) if so, whether it is detrimental or beneficial to India; and 
(d) if so, what steps Government are taking to prevent this carbon trade? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) With the coming into force of 
Kyoto Protocol February; 2005, Carbon Trade in some  Annex-l countries has 
substantially picked up. 
(b) The Kyoto Protocol provides for three mechanism s that enable the 
developed countries with quantified emission limita tion and reduction 
committments to acquire greenhouse gas reduction credits from activities 
134 

[16 March, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
outside their own boundaries at relatively lesser c osts. These are Joint 
Implementation, Clean Development Mechanism and Emission Trading. Under 
the Joint Implementation, a developed country with relatively higher costs of 
domestic greenhouse gas reduction activities would take up greenhouse gas 
reduction project activities in another developed c ountry, which may offer 
opportunities for greenhouse gas reduction activities at elsser costs. Under the 
Clean Development Mechanism, a developed country wo uld take up 
greenhouse gas reduction project activities in a de veloping country where the 
costs of greenhouse gas reduction project activitie s are usually much lower. 
Under Emission Trading, developed countries with qu antified emission 
limitation and reduction commitments under the Kyot o Protocol may acquire 
credits from other such Parties that do not need them for compliance with their 
own targets due to their actual emissions remaining lower than the upper limit 
provided for in the Protocol during the committment period of 2008-2012 and 
who, therefore, have a surplus of credits. 
(c) Carbon trade is beneficial for the India as our project proponent are able to 
sell Certified Emission Reductions to buyers in Annex-I countries that are Party 
to Kyoto Protocol. 
(d) Does not arise.

Statement II  
Measures to improve the nutritional status including Anemia  
Government has initiated various measures to improve the nutritional status 
including anemia in the population. The measures are: 
1. The Government of India has launched the Nationa l Rurai Health 
Mission (NRHM) in order to improve the availability  of and access 
to quality health care. Under this Mission, the Rep roductive and 
Child Health Programme (RCH-II) for Anemia Control,  provides 
iron and folic acid tablets to all pregnant and lac tating women 
and preschool children. 
The other important interventions under NRHM includ e Janani 
Suraksha Yojana wherein cash incentives are provided for delivering a child 
at the health institution. A village link worker (ASHA) who will orient 
the community on the importance of Nutrition and shall be provider of 
IFA tablets besides orienting the community on othe r health related 
issues. 
2. Supplementary feeding through programmes like In tegrated Child 
Development services scheme. Children in the age gr oup 0-6 yrs 
receive supplementary nutrition, immunization, pres chool 
education etc. Supplementary food to pregnant women /nursing 
mothers to the extent of 500 Calories and 20-25 gm protein per 
day is also provided along with nutrition and healt h education. 
One of the recent steps to increase the effectiveness of services 
153 

RAJYA SABHA [16 March, 2007] 
under ICDS is the provision of 50% of Recommended D ietary 
allowances (RDA) of micronutrients through supplementary food. 
Supplementary food is also provided through National Programme of 
Nutritional Support to Primary Education (Mid-day M eal 
programme) to school going children. 
3. A National Nutrition Policy was adopted in 1993 and the National Plan 
Action on nutrition is being implemented through va rious 
departments of Government of India. Now a National Nutrition 
Mission has been set up to deal with all nutritiona l problems 
through a Mission mode approach. 
4. Other measures initiated by the Government to impro ve the 
Nutritional Status of the people are: 
 
- Improving agricultural and horticulture produce. 
- Improving the purchasing power of the people throug h income 
generating schemes 
- Availability of essential food items at subsidised cost through 
Targeted Public Distribution system and Public Distribution system 
- Nutrition Education to increase the awareness and bring about desired 
changes in the dietary practices including the prom otion of breast 
feeding and dietary diversification 
5. Programmes for prevention of Specific Micronutri ent Deficienty 
disorders other than iron deficiency 
(i) Prophylaxis Programme to prevent Nutritional Blindness due to 
Vitamin A deficiency. This is also under the RCH programme (ii) 
National Iodine Deficiency disease Control Programme (NIDDCP) (iii) Pilot 
Programme for control of Micronutrient Deficiencies

Leprosy Societies have been formed in 27 major Stat es and District

a local media at periphery. 
(v) Training of General Health Care Staff and private- medical practitioners in 
leprosy diagnosis, treatment and disability prevention.

services at all levels through Simplified Informati on System (SIS) and

972 in 1901 to 927 in 1991. The sex ratio ha"s since gone up to 933 in 2001. In 
contrast the child sex ratio for the age group of 0 -6 years in 2001 is 927 girls 
per thousand boys against 945 recorded in 1991 Census. The Census 2001 figures 
further reveal that the child sex ratio is comparat ively lower in the affluent

per 1991 and 2001 Census is given in the enclosed Statement (See below),

been enacted to pre-ambit the use of such technolog ies, which significantly 
contribute to decline in sex ratio. Use of ultrasou nd machines has also been 
brought within the purview of the Act more explicitly so as to curb their misuse 
for detection and disclosure of sex of the foetus l est it should lead to female 
foeticide.

THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE, CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): Sir, Government have been 
concerned about the food security of the country an d the need to increase 
productivity in agriculture. We have also been concerned about the deteriorating 
terms of trade in agriculture. It is our commitment  that the farmers in this 
country will be given a better deal to ensure their well being and prosperity. Last 
year, we had no option to import Wheat to meet the needs of PDS and also the 
demands of the open market. 
The minimum support price for wheat in 2000-01 was Rs. 580. It was Rs 630 
in 2004-05, an increase of Rs 50 in four years. 
When this Government came to power, this short-sighted policy had started 
showing its impact on production. The wheat production had fallen to low levels of 
68 million tons in 2004-05. The production rose marginally to 69.35 million tons in 
2005-06. Last year the MSP was Rs. 650 over which we announced a bonus of 
Rs 50 per quintal. This year we followed it up with  an increase in MSP by 100 
rupees making it Rs. 750 per quintal. The farmers responded admirably and have 
increased the area under wheat and have also increase productivity. But for the 
unseasonal rain and hail storms, we would have benefited from a bumper crop. 
Government recognises this great effort. We are grateful to our farmers for this 
response. To give better returns to our farmers, Go vernment has decided to 
declare a bonus of Rs 100 per quintal for this Rabi season. This 
235 

RAJYA SABHA [16 March, 2007] 
is in addition to the increase in MSP announced already. This will mean that the 
farmers will get Rs. 850 per quintal of wheat against Rs. 700 last year. 
I sincerely hope that our farmers will welcome this announcement whole-heartedly 
and contribute more to our procurement operations. I would like to assure the 
farmers that the Government will do everything poss ible to support them get 
better returns from their land 
The Government is also committed to ensure that the re is no shortage of 
wheat in the country. To avoid any shortage in the country, the Government 
has also decided to permit duty free import of wheat till 31st December, 2007. 
The Government is committed to provide adequate foo d-grains to the poor 
sections of society, particularly the BPL and AAY through the public distribution 
system. It has also been decided that the Governmen t will import, if necessary, 
adequate quantities of wheat to meet the requirements of the Public Distribution 
System, and other welfare schemes like Mid Day meal s, ICDS, other 
employment and nutrition programmes etc. STC will b e asked to take 
preparatory steps to import upto 3 million tons in case of need.
